hints: Focus on polarity first, because $	ext{Br}_2$ is non-polar while $	ext{ICl}$ and $	ext{IBr}$ are both polar heteronuclear molecules.
Notice that $	ext{ICl}$ must have an extra type of force compared to $	ext{Br}_2$, which explains its much higher boiling point despite similar electron count.
Consider what changes between $	ext{ICl}$ and $	ext{IBr}$ when both are already polar, and think about electron cloud size and number of electrons.
walkthrough:
**Identify polarity and forces present**

All three are simple molecular substances, so boiling breaks intermolecular forces, not covalent bonds. $	ext{Br}_2$ is non-polar and has only instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces (London forces).

Forces present:
$$\text{Br}_2: \text{London only, ICl and IBr: London + permanent dipole-dipole}$$

**Explain why ICl boils higher than Br2**

$	ext{ICl}$ is polar because I and Cl have different electronegativities. That gives it permanent dipole-dipole attractions in addition to London forces.

$	ext{Br}_2$ has no permanent dipole, so $	ext{ICl}$ needs more energy to separate its molecules, giving 97 C versus 59 C.

**Explain why IBr boils higher than ICl**

Both $	ext{ICl}$ and $	ext{IBr}$ are polar, so both have permanent dipole-dipole forces. The key difference is now London forces.

Br is larger than Cl with more electrons, so $	ext{IBr}$ has a larger, more polarisable electron cloud. This gives stronger instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces.

**Check the permanent dipole trend**

In fact $	ext{ICl}$ is more polar than $	ext{IBr}$ because the electronegativity difference I-Cl is larger than I-Br. So $	ext{IBr}$ cannot boil higher due to stronger permanent dipoles.

The correct pair is therefore: permanent dipoles explain ICl > Br2, stronger London forces explain IBr > ICl.

options.A: Incorrect for the first comparison. $	ext{ICl}$ and $	ext{Br}_2$ have very similar total electrons, so London forces alone cannot explain the large jump from 59 C to 97 C. The new force is permanent dipole-dipole in polar $	ext{ICl}$.
options.B: Correct on both sides. $	ext{ICl}$ has permanent dipoles that $	ext{Br}_2$ lacks, so ICl > Br2. Both $	ext{ICl}$ and $	ext{IBr}$ are polar, but $	ext{IBr}$ has more electrons and a larger cloud, so stronger London forces make IBr > ICl.
options.C: Incorrect on both sides. It misses the permanent dipole that makes $	ext{ICl}$ different from $	ext{Br}_2$, and it reverses the second trend because $	ext{ICl}$ actually has the stronger permanent dipole due to larger electronegativity difference.
options.D: Correct for ICl > Br2 but wrong for IBr > ICl. $	ext{IBr}$ does not have stronger permanent dipoles than $	ext{ICl}$, it is less polar. Its higher boiling point comes from stronger London forces due to the bigger Br atom.
